outcome.shown: The seasons on Earth are primarily caused by the planet's axial tilt of approximately 23.5 degrees relative to its orbital plane around the Sun. As Earth orbits the Sun throughout the year, this tilt causes different hemispheres to receive varying intensities of direct sunlight at different times. When a hemisphere is tilted toward the Sun, it experiences summer due to longer days and more concentrated solar energy, while the hemisphere tilted away experiences winter due to shorter days and more indirect sunlight. Consequently, the cycle of seasons is a result of this constant orientation of the Earth's axis as it travels along its path.
